paragraphs: This is This Week in Congress, from Power to the People, for the week ending Saturday, October 3rd, 2026.
This briefing is read by a computer voice. Every fact in it comes from public records at Congress.gov, the House Clerk and Senate.gov.
The Senate held 12 recorded votes this week.
On Monday, the Senate passed the Protect College Sports Act of 2026, 77 to 22.
On Tuesday, a motion to take up Senate joint resolution 197 fell short, 48 to 51.
Also on Tuesday, a motion to bring Senate resolution 852 out of committee fell short, 47 to 51.
On Wednesday, a vote to begin debate on the Stop Insider Trading Act fell short of the votes needed, 53 to 47.
Also on Wednesday, a vote to begin debate on the Ratepayer Protection Act fell short of the votes needed, 57 to 43.
Also on Wednesday, the Senate voted to end debate on the nomination of Keith Sonderling, 53 to 47.
Also on Wednesday, the Senate confirmed Keith Sonderling to be Secretary of Labor, 47 to 41.
The Senate also held five other votes. Every vote is listed in the app.
The House held no recorded votes this week.

The Senate also passed 69 measures without a recorded vote. Among them were the MORE American Fuel Act of 2026, the Safe Access to Cash Act of 2026, and the Health Care Cybersecurity and Resiliency Act of 2026.
The House also passed 25 measures without a recorded vote.
One bill became law: the Kay Hagan Tick Reauthorization Act.
Coming up, the Senate next meets Monday, October 5th, 2026. The plan: convene for a pro forma session at 4:00 p.m. The House has not posted a floor schedule.
That's this week in Congress. You can read every bill and every vote in the app. Thanks for listening.
